questions.q: In ETL, when does the transformation step happen?
options: Before the data is loaded into the destination
After the data is loaded into the destination
At the exact same time as extraction
ETL doesn't include a transformation step
questions.explain: ETL stands for Extract, Transform, Load — the data is cleaned and reshaped in a separate engine before it ever lands in the destination.

questions.q: In ELT, where does the actual transformation happen?
options: Inside the destination system itself, after loading
Inside the source system, before extraction
It never happens — ELT skips transformation
In a separate engine sitting between source and destination
questions.explain: ELT loads raw data into the destination first, then uses the destination's own compute power (like a cloud warehouse) to transform it.

questions.q: Which pattern does Azure Data Factory lean toward by default in modern cloud architecture?
options: ELT — load raw data first, transform afterward
ETL — transform before loading, exclusively
Neither — Data Factory can't do either pattern
Data Factory only supports real-time streaming, not ETL or ELT
questions.explain: Data Factory supports both, but modern pipelines lean ELT-first — a Copy activity lands raw data in a lake or warehouse, then mapping data flows or an engine like Synapse handles the transform.

questions.q: What are mapping data flows an example of?
options: An ELT-style approach — staging data and transforming it with Spark after it's landed
A pure ETL engine that transforms data before any loading occurs
A scheduling tool with no relation to ETL or ELT
A reporting and visualization tool
questions.explain: Mapping data flows stage incoming data and apply Spark-powered transformations to it — fundamentally an ELT-style pattern, even inside a single activity.

questions.q: What are the two main reasons ELT overtook ETL as the default assumption in cloud data engineering?
options: Storage got cheap, and cloud warehouses got powerful enough to transform data efficiently themselves
ETL engines stopped being supported by any vendor
Regulations now require raw data to be loaded before transformation
ELT is the only pattern that supports on-premises data sources
questions.explain: Cheap storage removed the cost concern of keeping raw data around, and modern warehouses like Synapse Analytics can transform large datasets faster than a dedicated ETL engine.
